To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ocean-colour products derived from the merged data are consistent with in situ observations and with the quality of data from the individual sensors; that the uncertainties in the merged products are comparable to the uncertainties of individual sensors; that, for most of the ocean, the uncertainty in the merged product of remote-sensing reflectivity at the SeaWiFS wavebands is less than 0.002 sr-1, and the uncertainty in the chlorophyll-a product is less than 10%; and
(a) an ocean-colour climate time series has been generated for the period 1997 to 2018, and (b) the time series meets the climate user requirements.

a time series of remote-sensing reflectivity and chlorophyll concentration products for climate studies can be generated by merging data from multiple sensors, provided that: (a) the data are processed with algorithms that have been selected on the basis of their performance in climate studies, and (b) the products have been validated against in situ data and uncertainties have been quantified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation, validation, and characterisation of uncertainty in a long time series (1997–2018) of ocean-colour products at high spatial resolution (4 km), for use by climate scientists.
generating a long time-series of ocean-colour products that meet the requirements of climate research.
generating a consistent time series from data from multiple sensors; correcting for mean inter-sensor biases; and providing uncertainties for the products on a pixel-by pixel basis.

the Ocean-Colour CCI has delivered a time series of ocean-colour products that meet the requirements of the climate user community, and that the time series is now available for use in climate studies.

The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible, with careful selection of algorithms and data, and by following a rigorous approach, to generate an ocean-colour product time series that meets the requirements of the climate user community, and that can be used for a variety of applications, e.g., to study the role of phytoplanktons in the global carbon cycle, and to investigate their response to climate variability.
